faq: Which tools do you build the templates in?
Klaviyo, Mailchimp, Brevo, Omnisend and Shopify Email are the most common. We build with the tool's own editor so your team can edit without code.
Will you write the newsletter copy?
The designs include sample copy to show the layout. Writing your real emails is a separate service, but Premium includes building the first campaign using the text you give us.
Can you match an existing design?
Yes. Send a link or screenshot of your website or past emails, and we match the fonts, colors and spacing. We do not copy other brands' designs or use images you do not have rights to.
Will the design work in Outlook?
We build with simple layouts that hold up in Outlook, Gmail and Apple Mail. Some effects, such as rounded corners, may differ slightly in Outlook, and we show you the preview so you can see it.
desc:
Email newsletter design and template work gives your brand a layout that is easy to reuse and easy to read. Ecom Swift LLC builds branded templates inside your own email tool, with blocks your team can swap in minutes and checks on phones, desktops and dark mode.

## What is an email newsletter template?

An email newsletter template is a saved layout made of reusable blocks: a header with your logo, a hero image, text sections, product grids, buttons, an offer strip and a footer. You change the words and pictures, and the structure stays put. Each send looks like it came from the same business.

A template is different from a one-off design. A one-off can look lovely once and then fall apart when someone edits it. A template is built to be edited safely.

## Why layout shapes how people read your emails

Most subscribers glance at an email on a phone in a few seconds. If the text is tiny, the buttons are hard to tap or the images fail to load, they close it. A clear layout does the opposite: one main message at the top, a visible button, short blocks and enough spacing to read comfortably.

Consistent design also builds recognition. When your colors, fonts and tone repeat, readers know the sender at a glance and trust that the message is real. And a good template saves time, so your team spends the hours on the message instead of fighting the editor. We cannot promise that design alone changes clicks or sales, since content and offer matter too, but poor design reliably gets in the way.

## What a well-made newsletter design includes

- Your logo, fonts and colors applied consistently across every block.
- A single-column layout that stacks cleanly on narrow screens.
- Buttons large enough to tap with a thumb.
- Hero, text, image and product blocks that can be reordered.
- A product grid that pulls items from your store, where your tool supports it.
- Text sizes and color contrast that remain readable for most people.
- A dark mode check, so logos and backgrounds do not disappear.
- Alt text on images, so the message still makes sense when pictures are blocked.
- A footer with the required legal links and an unsubscribe link.
- Previews in several mail apps before the template is saved.

## How we build it

We begin with your brand: logo files, colors, fonts, and two or three emails you like. We build the template in your own tool, using its native editor so your team can maintain it later. Each block is tested with long and short text, so it does not break when real content goes in.

The Basic package delivers one branded template with hero, text and button blocks. Standard builds three layouts for news, products and sales, with a product grid, a dark mode check, inbox previews and an editing guide. Premium creates a fuller set of layouts and seasonal banners, adds accessibility checks and builds your first newsletter with your own content, followed by a handover call. Where a client wants an existing design copied, we match it as closely as the tool allows.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Lead with one clear message and one main button.
- Keep the layout narrow, around phone width.
- Use real text instead of text baked into images.
- Test the template with your longest product names.
- Keep the same footer in every send.

**Avoid:**
- Putting the whole email into one big image.
- Using many fonts and colors in a single message.
- Hiding the unsubscribe link.
- Cramming five offers into one email.
- Editing the template code by hand without a backup.

## Who it suits

A founder who has been sending plain emails and wants a cleaner look will benefit. A growing team with several people sending campaigns can use one template to keep the style steady. A store about to launch a seasonal campaign can prepare its banner set in advance.

## What we need from you

Send your logo, brand colors, preferred fonts, a few sample emails you admire and the name of your email tool. Tell us any wording or image rules. We never need your password. Access is given as a collaborator, staff or team user where the tool allows it, and you remain the owner of the account and templates.
